coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: MB4E
record.summary: A 398-unit, two-phase affordable housing development at 1290 3rd St on Mission Bay South Block 4-East, bounded by Mission Rock, Third and China Basin Streets, being developed by Curtis Development and Bayview Senior Services (Phase I through Mission Bay 4 East Associates, L.P.; Phase II through Mission Bay 4 East Associates 2, L.P.). OCII authorized an Exclusive Negotiations Agreement with them on September 3, 2024, with a term through September 3, 2027; as of OCII's February 3, 2026 resolutions, the Phase I ground lease and permanent loan agreement were still to be approved. Phase I (165 units, ~160 ft) is on the southern half of the block, facing China Basin St; Phase II (233 units, ~225 ft) is on the northern half, facing Mission Rock St.

open_questions: Whether the final parcel map has been recorded: the CEQA Notice of Exemption covers only the tentative map, and DataSF's parcels layer showed lots 8711029A and 8711029B (active) and no new lots for Block 4-East on 2026-10-12, so the Phase I and Phase II lots do not yet exist as separate Assessor parcels.

Affordability figures differ across sources and are not reconciled: the April 2026 CEQA Notice of Exemption says all residential units other than manager units "will be dedicated to lower-income households (earning no more than 70% of Area Median Income" (HUD and TCAC basis); the September 2024 ENA staff memo says 30-80% of AMI as defined by MOHCD, with a subset up to 95% MOHCD AMI; the developer's own project site (mb4e.com, undated, and mentioning a July 1, 2026 event) says 35% to approximately 95% of the area's median income. The binding restriction will be the TCAC regulatory agreements, which the Notice of Exemption says are to be recorded before building permits; no recorded agreement was found.

Construction start and completion dates are all expected dates, not events. The developer's own project site (mb4e.com, undated) gives Phase I construction start Q1 2027 and completion Q2 2029, Phase II start Q1 2028 and completion Q3 2030, pending financing. OCII's schedules of performance (Exhibit L to Resolutions 03-2026 and 04-2026) give estimated Notice to Proceed of February 2027 (Phase I) and February 2028 (Phase II) and estimated Certificate of Final Completion and Occupancy of July 2029 and October 2030.

Two of the February 2026 resolutions name the Phase I borrower "Mission Bay 4 Associates, L.P." (Resolution No. 02-2026's recital on the concurrent Phase I loan, and the resolving clause of Resolution No. 03-2026), apparently a slip; the September 2024 staff memo, the operative clause of Resolution No. 02-2026 and the loan agreement in Exhibit A to Resolution No. 03-2026 name it "Mission Bay 4 East Associates, L.P.", the name used here.

No public official's or community group's stated position on the project as a whole has been found and sourced. OCII's September 2024 staff memo records that OCII staff presented the recommended developer to the Mission Bay Citizens Advisory Committee on May 9, 2024 and "the MB CAC had no objections".

OCII's September 2024 staff memo and its attached RFQ say the site "is currently in use as a temporary parking lot without any structures" and "is currently serving as a surface parking lot", with termination of the parking operator's lease "anticipated for early 2027"; these are 2024 statements, and Pier & Point's own on-site observation of a parking lot on 2026-09-13 is not a published source. No cited document says whether the project is administratively separate from the Giants/Tishman Speyer Mission Rock masterplan; the memo mentions only modeling "bulk and tower separation restrictions similar to those applied to the Mission Rock project".

A City Spring 2026 development forecast was cited for the same schedule, but its document is no longer available at the published address and could not be read; the construction start dates rest on the developer's own site (mb4e.com: Phase I Q1 2027, Phase II Q1 2028, pending financing).

record.notes: MB4E -- 398-unit, 100% affordable (30-95% AMI per SF YIMBY, 2025) two-phase development (Phase I: 165 units/16 stories on the southern half of the block, facing China Basin and Third Streets; Phase II: 233 units/23 stories on the northern half, facing Mission Rock and Third Streets, per the 2026 OCII Notice of Exemption), plus an approximately 1,253 sq ft ground-floor retail space (same Notice of Exemption; SF YIMBY's 2025 article gave 1,280 sq ft), at 1290 3rd St (DataSF Parcels) on the block bounded by Mission Rock, Third and China Basin Streets. Developed by Curtis Development + Bayview Senior Services under SF's Office of Community Investment and Infrastructure (OCII) in the Mission Bay South Redevelopment Project Area. No cited source describes it as part of, or administratively separate from, the Giants/Tishman Speyer Mission Rock masterplan (the Verde/Canyon rows above), though it sits next to that area and faces a street named Mission Rock St. Site use: Pier & Point observed a surface parking lot here on the ground (2026-09-13); OCII's September 2024 staff memo and its attached RFQ also describe the site as a surface/temporary parking lot (a 2024 statement). Construction: the developer's project site (mb4e.com) lists Phase I construction start Q1 2027 and Phase II Q1 2028, pending financing, with bid packages through Q3 2026; a City Spring 2026 development forecast was cited for the same schedule, but its document is no longer available at the published address and could not be read. Not under vertical construction as of 2026-09-13 (Pier & Point's own observation), despite likely visible fencing/site-prep activity. NOTE: added after Pier & Point's own on-the-ground observation of this lot; the other facts were checked against OCII commission exhibits, the Notice of Exemption and DataSF parcel records. (mb4e.com; sfyimby.com/2025/06/renderings-revealed-for-23-story-affordable-housing-in-mission-bay-san-francisco.html)
